name: ErrorSaathi
statusNote: Built in a few hours at a hackathon. Some features are early prototypes (per its README).
summary: A CI doctor for open-source contributors. Give it a GitHub PR, a log or a screenshot and it explains what failed, why, and how to fix it in English or Roman Urdu, labelling every command SAFE, CAUTION or DESTRUCTIVE.

caseStudy.problem: First-time contributors see a red CI check, face a long and cryptic log, and give up. Documentation is mostly in English, and maintainers explain the same failures again and again.
approach: Fetch the PR, failed workflow jobs, job logs and diff from the GitHub REST API, or accept a pasted log, file or screenshot.
Clean the log, keep the lines around errors, and redact secrets before any model call.

A zero-cost regex router sends simple failures to a single fast call and complex ones through Triage, Investigator, Fixer and Safety Reviewer agents. A Blame agent maps errors to the changed file and line.

architecture.caption: Redaction happens before inference; posting needs explicit confirmation.

nodes.label: PR / log / screenshot
nodes.note: GitHub PR URL, pasted log, .log or .txt upload, or an error screenshot.

nodes.label: GitHub API
nodes.note: PR details, workflow runs, failed jobs, job logs and the diff.

nodes.label: Preprocess
nodes.note: Strip ANSI codes, collapse repeats, keep error windows, truncate long logs.

nodes.label: Redact secrets
nodes.note: Masks AWS keys, GitHub and GitLab tokens, JWTs, passwords, private keys, connection strings and emails.

nodes.label: Router
nodes.note: Regex detection of technology and signals. No API call.

nodes.label: Fast mode
nodes.note: One Gemma call for simple failures.

nodes.label: Multi-agent path
nodes.note: Triage, Investigator, Fixer, then Safety Reviewer.

nodes.label: Blame agent
nodes.note: Correlates errors with the PR diff to suggest the file and line.

nodes.label: Diagnosis
nodes.note: English or Roman Urdu, with SAFE / CAUTION / DESTRUCTIVE labels.

nodes.label: Confirm → PR comment
nodes.note: Posted only after the user previews and confirms.

decisions: A free regex router decides fast versus deep analysis before spending any model calls.
Two Gemma 4 models with automatic fallback, retries with backoff on 429 and 503, and a cache keyed on a hash of the redacted log.
Log windowing and truncation cut the tokens sent to the model.
security: Advise-only: the app never executes generated commands or changes infrastructure.
Destructive patterns such as rm -rf, kubectl delete and terraform destroy are flagged.
Keys live in git-ignored files; GitHub push protection and secret scanning are enabled on the repository (per README).
deployment: Runs with Streamlit locally; optional deploy to Streamlit Community Cloud with secrets in its settings.
A GitHub Actions workflow lives in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
limitations: AI output can be wrong and must be reviewed.
The Blame agent may not always find the exact file and line.
Very large logs are truncated, and free-tier model quotas limit throughput.
